question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{3}),$ calculate $P(X<2).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{3}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{e}^{-2x/3}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X<2)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{2}{3}{e}^{-2x/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-2x/3}{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-4/3}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.7364\end{aligned}
$$
